messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate in us-east-1 canary cluster. p95 latency up 3x. Paging oncall. source=canary-monitor rule=canary-error-rate threshold=1.5%

oncall-sre: I got paged, looking. grabbing logs from the canary nodes.

oncall-sre: @mrun @jlee can you two stand by? canary traffic was ~2% of rollout.

mrun: on it, pulling canary rollout history. I see last deploy included commit `c3f9b2e` which toggled `enable_new_kv_cache` flag in runtime.

jlee: thx. quick check: error spike aligns with that commit timestamp. stacktrace shows NPE in kv_cache when key length > 1024.

eng-runtime: seen the NPE in internal logs too. Root cause looks like missing length guard introduced in that tiny optimization. Reproducer attached.

oncall-sre: can we flip the feature flag off as a kill-switch?

jlee: we can. flag platform says this is a runtime-side flag; can flip immediately. Doing it now.

incident-bot: action=flag_change user=jlee flag=enable_new_kv_cache old=false new=false note="reverting accidental true in deploy"

oncall-sre: flag flip executed but errors still at ~60% of prior. some nodes still have cached state.

mrun: ok plan B: revert that single commit from canary deploy and redeploy. I can finish a revert PR in 10m and request fast-track.

sre-lead: +1 for revert. prefer single-commit revert rather than sweeping rollback since it's isolated. No customer-facing config change needed except rollout pause.

mrun: creating revert PR now. git commands:
```
# create revert commit
git checkout -b revert/c3f9b2e
git revert --no-edit c3f9b2e
# push and open PR
git push origin revert/c3f9b2e
```

mrun: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427 - requesting emergency merge. @sre-lead can you approve?

sre-lead: approved. merging and kicking off canary redeploy.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: runtime-service canary -> tag=staging-2026-03-15-2234 trigger=merge revert/c3f9b2e

support-swift: heads up, support saw two customers report increased 5xxs via support channel. ticket ids 6412, 6413. both are on EU region but routed through edge that hit us.

customer-ops: reaching out to affected accounts with incident notice and mitigation ETA. tagging customers for proactive outreach.

incident-bot: Canary deploy completed on 3 nodes. post-deploy checks running.

oncall-sre: metrics are improving. 5xx rate back to baseline across canary nodes. p95 latency normalizing.

eng-runtime: After revert logs show the NPE gone. pushing a small patch to add defensive length check to prevent regression in future. Will open PR for review (not blocking hotfix).

mrun: rolling out revert to prod in staged fashion now. deploy-bot will handle batch rollouts.

deploy-bot: Rollout to prod started: batch_size=25% interval=2m strategy=gradual

oncall-sre: monitoring dashboards. will pause if error rate > 0.5% above baseline.

15m_passed: (operator note) reached out to SRE rotation for handoff. @jlee taking next oncall window.

jlee: taking handoff, I will keep watch for next 30m. metrics look stable.

customer-ops: sent update to affected customers: brief summary, mitigation steps, and apology. No data exposure. Offering follow-up calls.

support-swift: tickets updated with status. customers acknowledged.

eng-runtime: created follow-up ticket to add unit test for long keys and add safe-guard: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/1789

oncall-sre: closing incident thread after 45m; final status: root cause commit c3f9b2e introduced missing guard, feature-flag flip + revert + single-commit rollback performed, customers impacted: small number (2 confirmed), no data loss, action items created.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: incident_id=INC-2026-2234 severity=sev2 duration=00:45:12 responders=[oncall-sre,mrun,jlee,eng-runtime,sre-lead,customer-ops,support-swift]

sre-lead: nice quick turnaround team. please post a short blameless postmortem and link in #postmortems. :thumbsup:"
